subject: Civil Engineering
title: Groundwater: The Hidden Reservoir
description: A micro-lesson that makes Groundwater: The Hidden Reservoir usable.

hook.text: There is 100 times more fresh water underground than in all rivers and lakes combined.

buildup.text: Aquifers are permeable rock or sediment layers that store and transmit groundwater.

discovery.text: Darcy's Law describes how fast water flows through soil — it depends on permeability.

twist.text: Overpumping drops the water table. In parts of India, wells must go 1,000 feet deeper.

climax.text: The Ogallala Aquifer supplies 30% of US irrigation water — and it's draining fast.

punchline.text: Underground water is invisible and finite. Deplete it and it's gone.

quiz.question: What does Darcy's Law describe?
options: The rate of evaporation from open water surfaces
The flow rate of groundwater through permeable soil or rock
The relationship between rainfall intensity and flood frequency

details.summary: Groundwater fills pores and fractures in underground rock and soil formations called aquifers, storing vast quantities of fresh water that supply wells, springs, and base flow to rivers.
details.whyItMatters: Groundwater provides drinking water to two billion people worldwide. Over-extraction causes wells to dry up, land to subside, and saltwater to intrude into coastal aquifers, threatening communities.
takeaways: Aquifers are geological formations that store and transmit significant quantities of water
Sustainable yield is the maximum extraction rate that avoids long-term aquifer depletion
Groundwater depletion causes land subsidence and saltwater intrusion in coastal areas

faq.question: What is the difference between confined and unconfined aquifers?
faq.answer: Unconfined aquifers have a water table open to atmospheric pressure and receive recharge directly from rainfall infiltration above. Confined aquifers are trapped between impermeable layers, are fully saturated, and under pressure greater than atmospheric.

faq.question: How do engineers determine sustainable groundwater extraction rates?
faq.answer: Pump tests measure aquifer transmissivity and storativity. Groundwater models simulate long-term extraction effects on water levels, stream flows, and neighboring wells. Sustainable yield balances extraction with natural recharge.
